rounds.fact: Charles Schwab was one of the first traditional brokerages to fully embrace online trading, helping legitimize the idea for investors who didn't trust newer online-only upstarts.
MSN launched alongside Windows 95 as Microsoft's answer to AOL, bundling a dial-up service with a portal homepage that shipped as the default for millions of new PCs.
Fox News launched its website alongside the cable channel in the mid-90s, and its early design leaned heavily on the bold red-white-and-blue branding that still defines the network today.
Encyclopedia Britannica put its entire encyclopedia online for free in 1999, a bold bet that ad revenue could replace its centuries-old subscription business, before pulling back a year later.
Newgrounds became the central hub for Flash animation and games in the early 2000s, launching the careers of several animators years before YouTube existed.
